items.1: Root split: five roots, a 32-byte root refused, and a found root whose P-256 seed is out of range
items.2: secp256k1 derivation and the symmetric field key, each equal to @bsv/sdk 4.0.1 (BRC-42, BRC-2)
items.3: P-256 derivation: private scalar and public key for three identifiers
items.4: ES256 round trip: exercised on record signatures by VA-SIG (verification, tampered signatures and a wrong signer's key)
items.7: Scalar rejection: a found P-256 identifier, and injected offsets 0, 1, n - 1, n, n + 1 and 2^256 - 1 on both curves through the `offset` hook
items.9: Derivation-identifier assembly: the KEYS §1.8.1 worked example
items.10: Key-path grammar: every registered purpose and variant accepted; an unregistered purpose, a foreign keyword, an empty segment, an extra segment and an over-long path refused; namespaces outside the profile refused
items.11: Profile conformance: the laboratory profile and ten non-conforming variants

K2.derivedFrom: SHA-512("TPNIL SDX v1 LAB_SELF_TEST_ONLY public test root: VA-KEY 2")

seed.by: components/sdx/p256/grind (seed): ikm = 0xff * 56 || uint64be(1557900713); its P-256 seed is at least n

path.by: components/sdx/p256/grind (path): the record identifier's last 16 characters are the Crockford base32 of 6019505901; the HMAC offset is at least n

decisions.text: Every value is computed under the laboratory profile `tpnil-sdx-lab:v1`: its labels, namespaces and key-path vocabulary are SDX's example values, used in the laboratory only, so the KEYS §1.8.1 worked example is also a laboratory known answer. Basis: KEYS §1.3.1, §1.12.

An HMAC offset of 0 or at least n is refused before any reduction, and the value is never reduced. Source finding: KEYS §1.8.2 both reduces the HMAC output modulo n and requires failure at or above n; KEYS §1.12 item 7 tests the rejection, which assumes the check comes first. Injected offsets travel through the optional `offset` hook, because no search can find 0 or n; an implementation without the hook is BLOCKED on those cases. Basis: KEYS §1.8.2, §1.12 item 7.

The secp256k1 symmetric key is the 32-byte x-coordinate of the shared point between the deriver's derived private key and the counterparty's derived public key, as BRC-2 and @bsv/sdk define it. Source finding: KEYS §1.8.2 says only that "the resulting shared material" is the key. Basis: KEYS §1.8.2, §1.8.4, §1.12 item 2.

Counterparty symmetry is tested in the KEYS §1.12 item 5 form: one side's derived public key equals the other side's derived private key's public key. Source finding: KEYS §1.8.4 and §2.14.1 say both sides derive the same private key, which the §1.8.2 algorithm does not give (coverage KEYS-1.8).

The `validate` operation applies the profile's five-level structure: keyword segments in their positions followed by one identifier each, level 4 only with a registered purpose, the session and delegation variants, no empty segment, and at most 1033 bytes; field names are bounded at 256 bytes (`labChoice`). Basis: KEYS §1.3, §1.6.1, §1.6.2, §1.12 item 10.

The laboratory profile reserves the rotation namespace and does not derive under it; a derivation request under it is refused (`labChoice`: KEYS §1.7 lets a profile reserve a role). Basis: KEYS §1.7, §1.10.3 step 5.

KEYS §1.12 item 4, the ES256 round trip, is exercised on record signatures by VA-SIG, which verifies signatures under a JOSE implementation in its generator and refuses tampered signatures and a wrong signer's key.

generator.deterministic: Every value is a function of the published roots and the profile.

oracles.generatorWitness: @bsv/sdk 4.0.1 KeyDeriver equals every secp256k1 derivation and the symmetric key.

node.dependencies: Node.js built-ins only (HKDF and HMAC by node:crypto, scalar multiplication by OpenSSL)

inline.purpose: The deployment profile under which TPNIL computes every SDX vector suite. KEYS §1.3.1 makes the strings that enter a derivation deployment parameters, and ENV §2.1 requires a deployment to publish its format identifier, protocol identifiers and key identifier grammar before its first write. This file publishes those values for the laboratory. No live deployment uses it, and nothing written under it is anything but test material.
inline.provenance: The namespace strings, per-curve labels, key-path keywords, purposes and credential type are the example values of the pinned SDX text, which KEYS §1.3.1 states are not normative. The laboratory adopts them for its own use only. The format identifier is the laboratory's own value; the example profile's `sdx:record:v1` is not used (ENV §2).

formatIdentifier.basis: ENV §2 (`proto`), ENV §2.1 first item, ENV §5.2 (the outer protected header carries the same value)

namespaceUse.rotation: Reserved and not derived under. Rotation envelopes sign under the signing namespace, which KEYS §1.7 permits (last rule) and KEYS §1.10.3 step 5 states.

curveLabels.basis: KEYS §1.3.1 item 2; KEYS §1.4.2 (example values; HKDF-SHA-256 info, empty salt, 32 bytes)

purposes.use: Per-field envelope encryption
Cross-domain handoff output lock, addressed to a named recipient
Funding top-up output lock; <n> is the output ordinal

keyPath.purposeSet: closed: a derivation boundary rejects any other level-4 purpose (KEYS §1.6.1)

recordKeyIdentifiers.basis: ENV §2.1 items 2 and 3; ENV §8.5, §8.6; KEYS §1.8.4; ANC §3.1
recordKeyIdentifiers.grammar: account/<accountId>/runtime/<runtimeId>/action/<actionId>. ENV §8.5 writes this shape as account/<account-id>/<writer-scope>/<writer-id>/record/<record-id> with profile-chosen literals; under this profile <writer-scope> is `runtime` and the record segment is `action` (reading R1).

signing.use: ES256 envelope signatures on P-256 (ENV §8.5) and audit-layer transaction signatures on secp256k1 (KEYS §1.8.4)

recipient.counterparty: self for the writer self-recipient, or the recipient's root public key

commitment.use: The per-record commitment key in the ANC §2.1 container (ANC §3.1)
commitment.root: the root keying material of the epoch the record's header declares in `ep` (ANC §3.1, §6.2 steps 3-4)

anchoring.basis: ANC §2.4: the floor is deployment configuration; the default is one unit of the smallest denomination

readings.reading: One level-3 keyword, `action`, names the record in every record-level key path on both curves: the ENV §8.5 signing key identifier, the ENV §8.6 recipient key identifiers, the secp256k1 audit-layer signing key and the ANC §3.1 commitment key. ENV's <writer-scope> is the KEYS level-2 keyword `runtime`.
readings.basis: KEYS §1.6.1 (a profile spells each keyword the same way everywhere), KEYS §1.8.4, KEYS §1.11.2 (one grammar for both curves), ANC §3.1 (the commitment key uses the signing scope and the grammar of KEYS). ENV §8.5 and §8.6 make the segment literals profile parameters.
readings.sourceFinding: KEYS §1.6.1 and §1.8.4 spell the level-3 keyword `action`. ENV §8.5 and §8.6 write `record` in the same position. Both are example values, so either is a valid profile choice, but the two pinned texts show different literals for one key path.

readings.reading: The laboratory publishes this one profile and computes every SDX suite under it. Its format identifier is `tpnil-sdx-lab:v1`. Its other strings are the SDX example values, used in the laboratory only. An implementation that cannot run under this profile is BLOCKED on byte-exact rows unless a vector set computed under its own published profile is admitted with an independent oracle.
readings.basis: KEYS §1.3.1 (a deployment fixes and publishes its profile), KEYS §1.12 (vectors are profile-relative), ENV §2 and §2.1 (no implementation should emit the example identifier)
